title: Linux staging maintainer rejects LLM cleanup patches but keeps a security exception
friendlyTitle: Linux sets limits on AI-made beginner patches
summary: Linux maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman said LLM-generated cleanup patches will be rejected from drivers/staging because that area is intended to teach new contributors. AI-found security fixes remain eligible when submitters test them on real hardware and can defend the result.
friendlySummary: The Linux staging area will reject AI-generated cleanup changes because it is a place for people to learn. Real security fixes can still be accepted if they are tested on actual hardware.
whyItMatters: The policy separates automation that bypasses learning from assistance that may uncover genuine harm. It offers a practical template for teams: define where AI is appropriate, require disclosure and evidence, and make the human submitter accountable for the output.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Teams can use a similar rule: allow AI where it helps, but require testing and a person who understands the result.
